meta.title: Thai Airspace Tour Guide
meta.tagline: From Bangkok sky to every shape that matters for rotorcraft pilots.

short.label: Express tour (~5 min)
short.description: Bangkok takeoff, then the capital-region volumes every hobby pilot should recognise first.

stops.title: Clearance — Bangkok
lines: Good morning from the Chao Phraya basin — Thailand's busiest sky starts right here.
We climb to sightseeing altitude so you can read the coloured cages before you ever spin a prop for real.

stops.title: Bangkok Control Zone
lines: That red drum is the Bangkok CTR — a 35 NM cylinder around Don Mueang and Suvarnabhumi.
It exists so airline jets can land in order. For drones: stay out entirely — CAAT expects ≥9 km from any airport, and this zone is much bigger than that.

stops.title: Bangkok Terminal Area
lines: Orange is the TMA — the arrival and departure shelf stacked above the CTR.
Pilots hear "Bangkok Approach" here. You won't, because you shouldn't be inside. Think of it as the airport's front garden in three dimensions.

stops.title: Bangkok City Restricted
lines: Purple means restricted — flight is allowed only with permission and conditions.
This 10 NM ring over inner Bangkok protects government and dense urban life. Your weekend vlog is not worth the paperwork.

stops.title: Chitralada Palace Restricted
lines: Small column, huge meaning — royal residences sit under their own restricted bubbles.
Even if your drone is tiny, the sensitivity isn't. Treat every purple disc near palaces as a hard no unless CAAT says otherwise.

stops.title: Muang Kom Prohibited
lines: Solid red is prohibited — the chart's way of saying "never without special authority."
These zones guard security sites. There is no casual waiver for content creators.

stops.title: Kanchanaburi Danger Area
lines: Deep orange danger areas flag hazardous activity — often military training west of Bangkok.
A drone might not trigger a jet, but you could wander into live ordnance or high-speed traffic. Respect the colour even when the sky looks empty.

stops.title: Ko Samet Restricted
lines: Islands get their own restricted caps — Samet is a tourist favourite and an airspace headache.
Beach beauty on the ground doesn't relax rules overhead. Check the chart before you launch from the sand.

stops.title: Sattahip Bay Danger
lines: Naval training boxes along the Gulf coast are danger areas for a reason — ships, aircraft, and weapons share the same slice of sky.
If you're mapping the Eastern Seaboard, give Sattahip a wide berth.

stops.title: Welcome to Explore
lines: You've seen the capital's greatest hits — controlled, restricted, prohibited, and danger.
Now the sticks are yours: fly manually, click any volume in the panel, press I to identify what you're looking at, and build the instinct charts teach.
Welcome to explore — fly curious, fly legal.

full.label: Full country tour (~22 min)
full.description: Takeoff at Bangkok, then every category and region rotorcraft pilots should appreciate — major airports, royal zones, islands, training areas, north and south.

stops.title: Clearance — Bangkok
lines: This is the full airspace story — not every one of 147 catalogued volumes, but every kind of rule you'll meet as a Thai drone pilot.
We depart Bangkok, climb, and warp coast to coast so the chart colours become places you remember.

stops.title: Bangkok Control Zone
lines: CTR — Control Zone — red on the chart, serious in real life. Thirty-five nautical miles around the capital's airline airports.
Utility: separates airline traffic from everything else. For you: no entry without ATC clearance you will never hold as a drone operator.

stops.title: Bangkok Terminal Area
lines: TMAs are the sequencing lanes where jets join and leave the CTR.
History: they grew with Suvarnabhumi's traffic boom. Utility: keeps arrivals ordered. Drone lesson: if you see orange near an airport, widen your buffer.

stops.title: Suvarnabhumi Control Zone
lines: Suvarnabhumi sits inside the wider Bangkok CTR — a reminder that big hubs can have nested cylinders.
The eastern approach path is busy 24/7. Your 250 g quad is invisible to radar until it isn't.

stops.title: Kamphaeng Saen Control Zone
lines: RTAF training bases carry their own CTRs — Kamphaeng Saen is the classic western training bowl.
Military utility: student pilots and tactical traffic. Civilian drone utility: stay far away; military ATC does not expect you.

stops.title: Bangkok City Restricted
lines: Restricted airspace is not a ban — it's "ask first, fly only if allowed."
Bangkok City's ring exists because low-altitude flight over parliament, ministries, and dense crowds is a security and privacy matter.

stops.title: Chitralada Palace Restricted
lines: Royal restricted areas are small on the map and enormous in law.
Utility: protect the monarchy and adjacent institutions. Appreciate them as precision purple pillars, not suggestions.

stops.title: Srapathum Palace Restricted
lines: Another palace cap — Bangkok has several. Together they teach that purple clusters are cumulative: obey each disc even when they overlap.

stops.title: Muang Kom Prohibited
lines: Prohibited means forbidden — the strongest word on the chart.
History: Cold War-era security mapping modernised for today's sites. Utility: absolute protection. Drone pilots should read red as "camera off, motors off."

stops.title: Kanchanaburi Danger
lines: Danger areas warn that something hazardous to aircraft may happen — bombing, firing, high-speed military traffic.
The western corridors date to RTAF exercises over Kanchanaburi and Suphan Buri. Empty sky can still be a classroom for jets.

stops.title: Suphan Buri Danger
lines: Neighbouring danger blocks often share one training story — check NOTAMs in real life; here we show the permanent AIP skeleton.
Appreciate danger as "maybe loud, maybe lethal" rather than "maybe empty."

stops.title: Ratchaburi Danger
lines: Coastal and river-adjacent danger areas protect firing ranges toward Myanmar and the Gulf.
If you film the floating market, check you're outside the orange before launch.

stops.title: Hua Hin Control Zone
lines: Resort towns still have CTRs — Hua Hin serves royal retreats and holiday traffic.
Utility: separates GA and airline ops from the beach. Your sunset shot from the pier must clear this cylinder first.

stops.title: U-Tapao Control Zone
lines: U-Tapao anchors the Eastern Economic Corridor — cargo, pax, and military share the coast.
Approximate boundary in this sim — always verify AD 2.VTBU in the live AIP before flying Rayong or Pattaya.

stops.title: Ko Hin Chalam Restricted
lines: Naval restricted caps hug Sattahip — small on the chart, tight in reality.
Utility: keep drones away from fleet movements and amphibious training.

stops.title: Sattahip Bay Danger
lines: Danger over the bay — live fire, aircraft, and ships.
History: decades of RTN training. Utility: national defence. Your takeaway: Gulf coast ≠ open playground.

stops.title: Sattahip Naval Base Prohibited
lines: Naval bases earn prohibited circles — no casual overflight, no "just quickly."
Red here is patriotism and safety rolled into one.

stops.title: Ko Samet Restricted
lines: Island restricted areas protect parks, radar, and naval reach around tourist hotspots.
Samet teaches that holiday geography ≠ exempt airspace.

stops.title: Phuket Control Zone
lines: Phuket CTR — southern tourism's front door to the skies.
International arrivals, GA, and helicopters share tight airspace over karst and sea. Plan launches from beaches outside the red.

stops.title: Phuket Terminal Area
lines: Orange TMA over the Andaman — sequencing for holiday jets.
Appreciate how TMAs extend offshore: your boat drone might still be under terminal airspace.

stops.title: Chiang Mai Control Zone
lines: Chiang Mai CTR guards the north's airline hub between mountains and valleys.
Utility: terrain-aware approaches for crewed aircraft. Drone utility: smoke, temples, and festivals still sit under this cap.

stops.title: Chiang Rai Control Zone
lines: Yellow Class D CTR — controlled, but lighter than Class C airline hubs.
Two-way radio for crewed VFR; drones still stay out. Note the colour: Class D is its own habit on the chart.

stops.title: Khon Kaen Control Zone
lines: Isaan's university hub has a CTR too — Thailand's airspace grid is nationwide, not just Bangkok-Phuket.
Rice fields look empty; charts say otherwise.

stops.title: Songkhla / Hat Yai Control Zone
lines: Deep south CTR — border trade and domestic links.
Reminder: Malay peninsula airspace is dense; cross-border shots need two countries' rules.

stops.title: Sattahip Naval Prohibited (RTN)
lines: Military prohibited zones — RTN weapon ranges drawn tight after AIP corrections.
Utility: fleet defence. Appreciate that military P areas can be smaller than danger but stricter.

stops.title: Nakhon Ratchasima Danger
lines: Large danger circles over Khorat — RTAF training heartland.
Fifty nautical miles sounds cinematic because it is. Drones do not belong in live-fire airspace even when it's dry season.

stops.title: Thailand Drone Rules — In Flight
lines: Register drones over 250 g with CAAT and NBTC.
Recreational ceiling 90 m AGL (~295 ft), daylight VLOS, no crowds or government roofs.
Stay ≥9 km from airports — and treat every coloured volume in this sim as the real neighbour it represents.

stops.title: Welcome to Explore
lines: You've warped the kingdom — CTR, TMA, Class D, restricted, prohibited, danger, military.
The catalog holds 147 volumes; you now know why they exist, not just where they sit.
Click any airspace, press I to identify, undo your flights, and go build the instinct. Welcome to explore.
